newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Lehman sees creeping economic improvement in Asia.
newsitem.headline: Lehman sees creeping economic improvement in Asia.

text.p: The 1996 slowdown in Asia's economic growth was largely cyclical and is coming to an end and with the omens improving, a broadening recovery could be underway, investment house Lehman Brothers said in a report.

"We are becoming more positive on Asia, expecting the external sector to propel a growth pick-up in the second half of the year," Lehman Global Chief Economist John Llewellyn wrote in Lehman's weekly Global Letter.
He added there were still some negative factors, but the dollar had reversed its (rising) trend, world trade signals were strong and demand for electronics was picking up.
Llewellyn said some of the 1996 problems still persisted.
"While the dollar has weakened vis-a-vis the yen, the progression has been volatile and the movement was interpreted by some as ambiguous at first," he wrote.
"China has not been recovering as strongly as some...had expected. The inventory overhang, while smaller, is still present, and capital spending remains sluggish," he added.
However, these influences did seem to be coming to an end, he wrote.
Despite its volatility, the yen/dollar rate was some 12 percent above its trough and had lowered the real effective exchange rates of the other Asian economies by similar amounts.

The NAPM (National Association of Purchasing Management of the United States) order index was signalling an expansion in the volume of U.S. imports and demand for electronics -- especially in the U.S. -- was picking up, he said.
"The volume effect will be important, but even more important to real incomes in Asia is the fact that semiconductor prices appear to have bottomed out," Llewellyn said.
"This stands to benefit (South) Korea and Singapore particularly, but others too will benefit in due course," he said.
"On balance, therefore, we are becoming more positive on Asia and expect to see the external sector propelling somewhat faster growth in the second half of this year," he added.
